name: Foo Fighters
summary: Allied bomber crews report glowing orbs following aircraft. Both Axis and Allies investigated. Neither side could explain them.
what: From late 1944, Allied B-17 and B-29 crews reported persistent glowing spheres tracking aircraft across two theaters. The objects matched aircraft speed, executed maneuvers no known aircraft could perform, and did not engage. The 415th Night Fighter Squadron logged 16 incidents. Axis pilots reported the same phenomenon — they thought they were Allied secret weapons.
why: Both sides investigated and concluded the objects were not their own or the enemy's. This mutual confusion rules out misidentification of known aircraft and establishes the phenomenon predates modern UAP awareness.
witnesses: Hundreds of Allied and Axis aircrew. Multiple formal military reports filed.
evidence: Declassified mission debriefing reports from multiple squadrons. Consistent accounts from adversarial nations.
response: Both Axis and Allied high commands investigated. No explanation was ever reached. Files classified after the war.

name: Roswell Incident
summary: USAF issues press release confirming "flying disc" recovery. Retracted within 24 hours. Three cover stories follow across 47 years.
what: On July 8, 1947, RAAF public information officer Walter Haut issued a press release stating the 509th Bomb Group had recovered a "flying disc." Within 24 hours, General Roger Ramey held a press conference with a weather balloon — cover story 1. In 1994, the Air Force issued Project Mogul — cover story 2. A 1997 report said the "alien bodies" reports came from crash test dummies — cover story 3. Those dummies weren't used until 1953.
why: Three contradictory official explanations over 47 years is the documented suppression signature. George Knapp testified to Congress in September 2025 that Bigelow negotiated with a Lockheed executive over material held at a California facility described as having composition "suggesting it had been crafted in a zero-gravity environment."
witnesses: Mac Brazel, multiple 509th personnel, Sheriff George Wilcox, Dr. Jesse Marcel Sr. Multiple deathbed testimonies from base personnel.
evidence: Original RAAF press release (July 8, 1947). Three contradictory official explanations. Congressional testimony about Lockheed material. Multiple military deathbed affidavits.
response: Cover story 1: weather balloon (1947). Cover story 2: Project Mogul classified balloon (1994). Cover story 3: crash test dummies (1997). Dummies not used until 1953.

name: Lubbock Lights
summary: V-formation photographed multiple times by engineering student. Thousands witness across city. Project Blue Book: Unknown.
what: Between August and October 1951, residents of Lubbock Texas observed multiple formations of soft blue-green lights passing overhead at high speed. Texas Tech student Carl Hart Jr. photographed the formation on multiple occasions. Project Blue Book classified the case as "unknown."
why: One of Project Blue Book's highest-profile unresolved cases. Hart's photographs were analyzed by Air Force experts and found to be unaltered. No conventional explanation was ever proposed.
witnesses: Thousands of residents. Texas Tech professors. Carl Hart Jr. (photographer).
evidence: Multiple authenticated photographs. Project Blue Book "unknown" classification.
response: Project Blue Book investigated and classified Unknown. No conventional explanation proposed.

name: Malmstrom Missiles
summary: 10 nuclear ICBMs go offline simultaneously during UAP overflight. USAF confirms deactivation but cannot explain mechanism.
what: On March 16, 1967, Capt. Robert Salas was on duty in the underground launch control center when security personnel radioed to report a glowing red object over the front gate. As the conversation continued, all 10 Minuteman I ICBMs went offline simultaneously — a status that cannot happen through any known malfunction chain.
why: Simultaneous shutdown of 10 ICBMs represents an operational failure mode Air Force engineers could not replicate. The USAF confirmed the missiles deactivated but disputes UAP causation — having never explained the actual mechanism. Peer-reviewed statistical analysis: p=0.00013.
witnesses: Capt. Robert Salas. Multiple security personnel. Adjacent flight experienced the same event.
evidence: USAF confirmation of deactivations. Air Force report cannot explain simultaneous shutdown. Multiple officer testimony under oath.
response: USAF confirmed deactivations occurred. Disputed UAP causation. Never explained the mechanism. Witnesses instructed not to discuss.

name: Tehran F-4 Incident
summary: Two F-4 Phantoms scrambled. Weapons systems disabled on approach. DIA declassified the report.
what: On September 19, 1976, two Imperial Iranian Air Force F-4s were scrambled to intercept a UAP over Tehran. As the first F-4 attempted to arm its weapons on radar lock, all weapons systems and communications failed simultaneously. The second F-4 experienced identical failures on its approach.
why: The DIA declassified the report, making Tehran one of the few UAP cases with both a declassified intelligence report AND surviving military testimony. The weapons disablement pattern is consistent across Malmstrom, Usovo, and multiple other incidents — indicating deliberate interference, not malfunction.
witnesses: IIAF pilots. Ground radar operators. DIA report documented all witness accounts.
evidence: DIA declassified report. Iranian Air Force records. Multiple radar tracks.
response: DIA classified the report. Released via FOIA decades later.

name: Shag Harbour
summary: Object crashes into harbor. Government officially classifies as unknown origin. Tracked 25 miles underwater to SOSUS array. Never reclassified in 57 years.
what: On October 4, 1967, multiple witnesses including RCMP officers observed an object descend at 45° and enter Shag Harbour. An 80ft yellow foam slick appeared. The Royal Canadian Navy deployed HMCS Granby. Fleet Diving Unit Atlantic searched for 3 days. Sonar contacts indicated the object traveled approximately 25 miles underwater to Government Point — the site of a SOSUS submarine listening network.
why: The best-documented transmedium event in history. The Canadian government has never changed its classification. An object that enters the ocean and strategically positions itself next to North America's most sensitive submarine-tracking network is not behaving randomly.
witnesses: 11+ confirmed witnesses including RCMP. Coast Guard crew.
evidence: Royal Canadian Navy incident report. 80ft foam slick. Library and Archives Canada file — never reclassified. Swept-clean seafloor depressions found by civilian diver decades later.
response: Navy deployed HMCS Granby. Fleet Diving Unit searched 3 days. Official classification: "unknown origin." Never reclassified.

summary: 500+ photos. 16hrs footage. Hundreds of civilians injured by light beams. Captain sees beings inside craft. Dies 2 months after speaking.

Captain Hollanda Lima saw beings inside the craft through transparent sections — gave one interview after his secrecy oath expired and died of a cardiac event at 45, two months later, with no cardiac history.

name: Rendlesham Forest
summary: USAF nuclear base. 3 nights. Radiation confirmed on Lt Col Halt's real-time tape. UK paid VA settlement citing own UAP radiation study.
what: Over three nights in December 1980, USAF personnel from RAF Bentwaters and Woodbridge — a nuclear weapons storage facility — observed craft in Rendlesham Forest. Deputy Base Commander Lt. Col. Charles Halt led a ground team with Geiger counters. His real-time audio recording documents elevated radiation readings and craft moving through the forest.
why: The UK government paid a medical settlement to Airman John Burroughs in 2015, citing its own Project Condign study — a classified report confirming UAPs produce plasma radiation effects. You cannot compensate someone for UAP radiation injuries while simultaneously claiming nothing happened. The settlement is the admission.
witnesses: Lt. Col. Charles Halt. Multiple USAF personnel over 3 nights. Halt's real-time audio is public record.
evidence: Halt memo to UK MoD (declassified). Real-time audio recording. Radiation readings from military Geiger counter. Ground indentations. 2015 VA settlement.
response: MoD: "no defense significance." Internal Project Condign study confirmed radiation. 2015 VA medical settlement paid.

summary: GEIPAN + INRA confirmed: 4-5 ton compression, 600°C heat, mineral deposits, plant cellular collapse. The gold standard of physical evidence.

These findings cannot be explained by any conventional landing event.

response: Soviet military classified the incident. SETKA program documented it. Became known in the West only after Soviet collapse.

name: Belgian Wave
